cells.tense: You're letting go right now, and the timing is yours — you're the one with the pen.
cells.verb: You're letting what's finished actually finish, and you can feel the rightness of it as you do it.
cells.place: What's arriving is landing on you — not handed to you, not forced on you; you're meeting it as it comes.
cells.ask: Offer the next ending the same plain trust you gave the last one — and let fair exchange flow back in, give and take in even current.
cells.core: You're letting something end, and you're doing it cleanly — not dragged, not rushed, at the pace it actually takes. What's over is over, and you're not pretending otherwise. That kind of release only reads as loss from outside; from where you're standing it reads as making room. What's arriving next has somewhere to land because you cleared it.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting it end, and the ending is clean.

cells.tense: You're already bracing for what you'll tear down next, before the present one has a chance to finish.
cells.verb: You're cutting things loose ahead of schedule — ending before the living part is done, mistaking motion for freedom.
cells.place: What's arriving gets met with a plan to dismantle it; you're standing at the door with your hands already on the frame.
cells.ask: Let one thing stay whole a little longer than your fear wants — stay close enough to the person in front of you to feel what they feel, without losing where you end and they begin.
cells.core: There's a version of this in your future where the next ending finally frees you, and you're living there now — so everything that's here gets treated as something to clear. You call it liberation. The people around you can feel the cost. Turning over that fast doesn't leave anything standing long enough to be loved.
cells.sheetLine: You're ending things ahead of schedule and calling it freedom.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed behind you, and you've been there a while.
cells.verb: You're holding on to what's already finished — keeping the shape of something that stopped being alive.
cells.place: What's arriving has to get past the things you won't set down; the entryway is crowded with what you're carrying.
cells.ask: Let one direction come from what you actually feel this week — not from duty, not from habit; following genuine want is what gets the current moving again.
cells.core: Something in you has ended and you haven't let it. You call it loyalty, and maybe some of it is — but underneath the loyalty there's a fear of what happens if you stop tending a thing that's already gone. Keeping it warm costs you the room it's standing in. The empty space isn't a loss; it's what you need in order to take in anything new.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping something warm that's already gone.

cells.tense: Something in you is already ending, and you'd tell me nothing is changing.
cells.verb: The clearing is happening, but you haven't picked up the pen — you talk about it like weather.
cells.place: What's arriving is already inside you; you just haven't named it as arriving.
cells.ask: Put a shape on one thing that's shifting in you — say plainly what's changing and what you're going to do about it, so what you organize holds and things make sense to the people around you.
cells.core: You're not waiting for a sign — the change has already started, in what you've stopped reaching for and what you no longer say yes to. None of it has been claimed as yours. Talking about a thing as if it's happening to you, when it's happening because of you, leaves you with none of the say in it and none of the relief of a real ending.
cells.sheetLine: It's already changing. You're talking about it like weather.
